proposals.before: His grandfather Longdao had been northern inspector of Yan Province under Song.
proposals.after: His grandfather Longdao had been inspector of Northern Yan Province under Song.
proposals.reason: 北兗州 is the province name Northern Yan (Northern Yanzhou), not a northern posting in Yan Province.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wen took up post at Xia Province, he made Hui recording secretary adjutant and concurrently chief clerk of the commandery office.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wen took up post at Xia Province, he made Hui recording secretary adjutant and concurrently chief clerk of the headquarters.
proposals.reason: 府主簿 is clerk of the headquarters staff, not of a commandery (郡).

proposals.before: In the tenth year he was moved to supervising secretary and attendant at the gates.
proposals.after: In the tenth year he was moved to Supervising Secretary and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
proposals.reason: 給事黃門侍郎 is a single Yellow Gate office; the English splits it and drops 黃門.

proposals.before: Hui was scrupulous and wary of corruption; he hung a portrait of Yang Zhen in his sleeping room to keep himself honest.
proposals.after: Hui was scrupulous and wary of corruption; he painted a portrait of Yang Zhen in his sleeping room to keep himself honest.
proposals.reason: Chinese 畫楊震像 means he painted (or had painted) Yang Zhen's likeness, not merely hung a ready-made portrait.

proposals.before: They said to one another, "These are Prefect Shen's own lines."
proposals.after: They said to one another, "This is Prefect Shen's own handwriting."
proposals.reason: 手跡 means autograph or handwriting, not the poem's 'lines' as verse.

proposals.before: He served as junior minister of works and junior guardian, went out as inspector of Jing Province, and returned as junior minister of worship and junior minister of ritual.
proposals.after: He served as junior minister of works and junior guardian, went out as inspector of Jing Province, and returned as junior minister of the masses and junior minister of ritual.
proposals.reason: 小司徒 is the junior Minister of the Masses (司徒), not a minister of worship; 小宗伯 already covers ritual.

proposals.before: Lu Tong also marched when the siege of Luoyang was lifted.
proposals.after: Lu Tong again took part in lifting the siege of Luoyang.
proposals.reason: 又從解洛陽圍 is active participation in raising the siege, not a march that merely coincided with the siege already being lifted.

proposals.before: Emperor Wen once said to him at leisure, "You are already mild and generous—why style yourself Hero of the Age?
proposals.after: Emperor Wen of Wei once said to him at leisure, "You are already mild and generous—why style yourself Hero of the Age?
proposals.reason: Chinese 魏文帝 is specifically the Wei emperor, not the Zhou posthumous Emperor Wen; the idiomatic rendering drops 魏.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tianhe Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husiwen Lue and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly visit.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husi Wenlüe and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly visit.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the reign name with Qi; 斛斯 is the surname Husi and 文略 the given name, not Husiwen Lue.

proposals.before: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husiwen Lue and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly mission.
proposals.after: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husi Wenlüe and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly mission.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise fuses the Xianbei surname 斛斯 with the given name 文略.

proposals.before: Before coming of age he entered service as regular attendant of scattered cavalry outside the office.
proposals.after: Before coming of age he entered service as supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.reason: 員外 marks an extra-quota (supernumerary) post, not a location 'outside the office'; 散騎侍郎 is the cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, not 'scattered cavalry'.

proposals.before: 〔Jian〕 recorder.
proposals.after: Concurrently recorder.
proposals.reason: 兼記室 means he concurrently held the recorder post; the literal rendering imports the previous unit's emendation marker 'Jian' and omits 兼.

proposals.before: When Wei Chijiong marched against Shu, Min was made campaign army marshal.
proposals.after: When Yuchi Jiong marched against Shu, Min was made campaign army marshal.
proposals.reason: 尉遲迥 is the Xianbei surname Yuchi plus given name Jiong; 'Wei Chijiong' splits the surname as if 尉 were Wei.

proposals.before: When Wei Chijiong campaigned against Shu, Min was made army marshal on campaign.
proposals.after: When Yuchi Jiong campaigned against Shu, Min was made army marshal on campaign.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of the surname 尉遲 as 'Wei Chi' in the literal English.

proposals.before: Once Sheng was made grand guardian, Rou joined his staff as a general of the victorious army.
proposals.after: When Sheng was made grand guardian, Rou was made his staff officer (yuan) and given the added rank of Champion General.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以柔為掾，加冠軍將軍 records two acts: appointment as 掾 and added 冠軍將軍, not a single fused generalship; 冠軍將軍 is the Champion General title.

proposals.before: Learning they were Rou's composition, he sent a palace attendant with condolences and also bestowed silk and brocade.
proposals.after: Learning they were Rou's composition, he sent a palace attendant with greetings and also bestowed silk and brocade.
proposals.reason: 勞問 is a courtesy inquiry or consolation greeting, not funeral condolences.

proposals.before: Soon he was deputy envoy on a marriage mission to Chen.
proposals.after: Soon he was deputy envoy on a diplomatic mission to Chen.
proposals.reason: 聘陳 is a court embassy to Chen, not specifically a marriage mission.

proposals.before: Tang Jin, courtesy name Fulai.
proposals.after: Tang Jin, courtesy name Fulin.
proposals.reason: 附璘 transcribes as Fulin, not Fulai.

proposals.before: Tang Jin, styled Fulai.
proposals.after: Tang Jin, styled Fulin.
proposals.reason: 附璘 transcribes as Fulin, not Fulai.

proposals.before: He took part in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, had merit in both, and was enfeoffed viscount of Guniang county.
proposals.after: He took part in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, had merit in both, and was enfeoffed viscount of Guzang county.
proposals.reason: 姑臧 is Guzang, not Guniang.

proposals.before: Following in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, he had merit in both and was enfeoffed viscount of Guniang county.
proposals.after: Following in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, he had merit in both and was enfeoffed viscount of Guzang county.
proposals.reason: 姑臧 is Guzang, not Guniang.

proposals.before: He was transferred to minister of the grand commissariat, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.
proposals.after: He was transferred to minister of revenue, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.
proposals.reason: 戶部尚書 is minister of revenue, not the grand commissariat.

proposals.before: He was transferred to minister of the grand commissariat, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry, opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.
proposals.after: He was transferred to minister of revenue, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry, opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.
proposals.reason: 戶部尚書 is minister of revenue, not the grand commissariat.

proposals.before: At that time Duke of Yan Yu Jin had high merit and great renown and was the hope of court and country.
proposals.after: At that time Yu Jin, Duke of Yan, had high merit and great renown and was the hope of court and country.
proposals.reason: 燕公于謹 is Yu Jin, Duke of Yan; the fused English order is misleading.

proposals.before: [variant: xiá]
proposals.after: [emended reading: 暇, leisure]
proposals.reason: The unit is a textual note supplying 暇 as the emendation behind 休假, not an English gloss 'variant: xiá' that omits the meaning.

decisions.reason: 宋北兗州刺史 names the inspectorate of Northern Yan Province (北兗州), not a northern posting in Yan Province.
兼府主簿 is concurrent chief clerk of the headquarters (府), not of a commandery (郡).
給事黃門侍郎 is one Yellow Gate office; the original splits it and omits 黃門.
畫楊震像於寢室 is painting (or having painted) Yang Zhen's likeness, not hanging a ready-made portrait.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃畫楊震像於寢室以自戒

decisions.reason: 手跡 means handwriting or autograph, not the poem's verse lines.
入為小司徒、小宗伯 pairs junior Minister of the Masses with junior minister of ritual; 小司徒 is not a minister of worship.
又從解洛陽圍 means he again took part in raising the Luoyang siege, not that he merely marched as it was already lifted.
魏文帝 specifies the Wei emperor; dropping 魏 would conflate him with Zhou's posthumous Emperor Wen.
斛斯文略 is surname 斛斯 plus given name 文略; the original fuses them as Husiwen Lue and also runs Tianhe into Qi.
The literal line likewise mis-segments 斛斯文略; Husi Wenlüe restores the Xianbei surname and given name.
員外散騎侍郎 is a supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, not scattered cavalry posted outside an office.
兼記室 is concurrent recorder; 〔Jian〕 wrongly imports the previous unit's emendation and drops 兼.
尉遲迥 is Yuchi Jiong; Wei Chijiong wrongly splits the two-character surname 尉遲.
The literal English repeats the same mis-split of 尉遲 as Wei Chi.

decisions.after: When Sheng was made grand guardian, Rou was made his staff officer and given the added rank of Champion General.
decisions.reason: 以柔為掾，加冠軍將軍 is two acts, 掾 plus Champion General; the original fuses them and mistranslates 冠軍將軍. The proposal is right in substance but the parenthetical (yuan) is an awkward gloss, so the sentence is recast without it.
遣舍人勞問 is a courtesy greeting or inquiry, not funeral condolences.
聘陳 is a court embassy to Chen, the same diplomatic 聘 as 來聘, not a marriage mission.
字附璘 transcribes as Fulin; Fulai invents a wrong reading of 璘.
The literal courtesy-name likewise misreads 附璘 as Fulai rather than Fulin.
姑臧縣子 is viscount of Guzang county; Guniang misreads 臧.
The literal enfeoffment likewise requires Guzang for 姑臧, not Guniang.
戶部尚書 is minister of revenue, not minister of the grand commissariat.
The literal office title likewise mistranslates 戶部尚書 as grand commissariat.
Duke of Yan Yu Jin already names 燕公于謹 with the correct title and person; reordering to Yu Jin, Duke of Yan is only stylistic.
The unit is an emendation of 休假 with 暇 “leisure,” not a pinyin-only variant gloss; the proposed replacement still put a Chinese character into the English field.

claimRevisions.reason: The restored English for 魏文帝 must keep Wei; Emperor Wen alone matches the separate 文帝 alias, not this form.
The English personal name Husiwen Lue was produced only by mis-segmenting 斛斯文略; the source supports Husi Wenlüe.
Wei Chijiong exists only in the bad split of 尉遲迥; the personal name is Yuchi Jiong.
English Fulai was created by the mistranscription of 附璘; the courtesy name is Fulin.
